sample.description:
Overall radio conditions show a consistently weak downlink reference signal with RSRP ranging between -113.0 dB and -112.0 dB. The average RSRP is -112.0 dB. Uplink modulation is relatively high with UL_MCS spanning 13.0 to 17.0 and an average of 16.5, while downlink MCS is fixed at 7.0. DL_BLER varied from 0.00087 to 0.048 with a mean of 0.013. UL_BLER was much higher, ranging from 0.62 to 1.0 with a mean of 0.89.

Uplink resource allocation and quality show bursts: UL_NPRB rose sharply in two periods (peaking around 66.46 and 73.39) and overall spans 38.3 to 82.5 with a mean of 55.9. UL_SNR is healthy, between 16.6 dB and 23.1 dB with a mean of 20.0 dB. PRBs on the downlink experienced multiple large spikes and drops (the largest spike reached 63.4); PRBs_DL_Current covers 0 to 63 with a mean of 16.2. PRBs_UL_Current stayed low, between 0 and 3.1 with a mean of 0.78. Downlink PRB utilization oscillated substantially (range 38.4 to 90.8) with a mean of 59.9, while uplink PRB utilization was steadier between 34.9 and 55.3 with a mean of 45.3.

Traffic and buffer metrics indicate significant uplink backlog: Estimated_UL_Buffer ranged from 199,740.3 KB to 205,288.4 KB with a mean of 203,500.0 KB. Transmit bytes varied widely from 29 Bytes to 62,299 Bytes with a mean of 15,724.5 Bytes; receive bytes ranged from 19 Bytes to 2,620 Bytes with a mean of 636.8 Bytes. Packet rates were moderate: UL_NumberOfPackets between 236.7 and 353.8 (mean 289.2), DL_NumberOfPackets between 289.7 and 482.9 (mean 374.9).

Finally, the observed transport was overwhelmingly TCP in both directions, with TCP present for 98.44% of timestamps.

- **Issue:** Gradually worsening uplink buffer overflow in the wireless network.
- **Symptoms:** Exponential growth in uplink buffer backlog and block error rates; logarithmic decay of transmitted and received bytes; linear increase in uplink and downlink packet counts; logistic growth in PRB utilization and PRBs allocated.
- **Root Cause:** Persistent mismatch between offered uplink traffic load and available uplink capacity, likely due to sustained congestion or misconfigured scheduling/resource allocation.
- **Resolution:** Increased uplink resource allocation, optimized scheduling parameters, and temporarily throttled uplink traffic to restore buffer stability and reduce error rates.

sample.description:
RSRP showed notable degradations, with measured values falling as low as -136.0 dB (minimum) and reaching up to -116.0 dB (maximum). The average RSRP was -121.4 dB. Two pronounced drops occurred: one down 17.0 dB (to −136.0 dB) and another down 9.34 dB (to −131.34 dB), indicating intermittent weak downlink coverage.

Uplink modulation (UL_MCS) was highly variable, ranging from 0 to 17 with a mean of 11.4. The largest abrupt change was a 15.0-point fall to 0, reflecting periods where uplink spectral efficiency collapsed. Downlink modulation (DL_MCS) ranged between 2.3 and 7.0, with a mean of 6.0, and experienced a modest dip of 3.69 to 2.31.

Downlink block error rate (DL_BLER) fluctuated between 0.072 and 0.66, averaging 0.29, and exhibited multiple spikes—the largest jump increased by 0.40 to 0.50—signaling intermittent downlink reliability issues. Uplink BLER varied from 0.012 to 0.17 with a mean of 0.076, indicating generally better uplink link reliability than downlink.

UL_NPRB (uplink assigned PRBs) spanned 5.0 to 39.0 with a mean of 14.5; a rapid increase of 28.20 to 37.84 occurred, showing transient high uplink resource allocation. PRBs_DL_Current ranged from 0 to 59 with a mean of 19.2 and experienced multiple large swings, including a spike of 58.6 to 59.4, reflecting bursts of downlink scheduling. PRBs_UL_Current ranged 0 to 22 with mean 1.9. DL PRB utilization ranged 0 to 56 with mean 18.1 and mirrored the downlink PRB spikes; UL PRB utilization ranged 0 to 21 with mean 1.8 and had a jump of 19.62 up to 20.75, indicating short uplink load bursts.

UL_SNR remained relatively healthy, between 13.6 dB and 27.5 dB with a mean of 20.5 dB. Traffic volumes showed large uplink bursts: TX_Bytes varied from 0 to 360,000 Bytes (max ~3.63e+05) with a mean of 100,083.9 Bytes and exhibited two large spikes to ~323,782 and ~362,930 Bytes. RX_Bytes ranged from 0 to 25,000 Bytes (max ~2.5e+04) with a mean of 3,281.6 Bytes. The Estimated_UL_Buffer spanned 0 to 1,500 Kilobytes with a mean of 205.5 KB, indicating occasional uplink queuing.

Packet counts reflected bursty behavior: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 95 (mean 20.4) and DL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 210 (mean 62.4). Transport-layer usage was dominated by TCP: DL_Protocol was TCP for 92.97% of timestamps and UL_Protocol was TCP for 89.84% of timestamps (UDP negligible).

Overall, the dataset shows intermittent coverage and downlink reliability degradation (low RSRP, elevated DL_BLER and MCS drops) coupled with episodic uplink resource and traffic surges (PRB/UL_NPRB jumps, large TX_Bytes spikes) while UL_SNR remained broadly acceptable.

**Diagnose Summary:**
- **Issue:** Severe Doppler shift causing periodic wireless signal and throughput instability.
- **Symptoms:** Periodic fluctuations in RSRP (3–8 dB) and uplink SNR (2–5 dB) at 2–3 Hz; downlink and uplink MCS decreased by 1–2 levels; multiplicative oscillations in transmitted/received bytes (factor 0.20–0.40) and PRBs allocated (factor 0.30–0.60) at 2–3 Hz.
- **Root Cause:** Rapid relative motion between the transmitter and receiver inducing Doppler effect.
- **Resolution:** Reduced source/receiver mobility, reoriented antennas for optimal alignment, and updated scheduling/adaptation algorithms to improve performance under mobility scenarios.

sample.description:
Overall RF conditions were moderate with intermittent volatility. RSRP varied between -122.4 dB and -105.9 dB; the average RSRP was -111.7 dB. Several abrupt RSRP transitions occurred (at least six), the largest movement reaching -106.6 dB around the noted interval. Uplink SNR ranged from 11.5 dB to 21.7 dB with a mean of 18.0 dB, supporting relatively healthy uplink link quality.

Uplink MCS stayed tightly clustered between 16.0 and 17.0 (mean 16.4), while downlink MCS ranged from 6.0 to 7.0 (mean 6.8). Downlink BLER was very low, between 0 and 0.0052 (mean 0.0004). Uplink BLER was higher, spanning 0.068 to 0.16 with a mean of 0.10, indicating some uplink retransmissions risk.

Resource usage showed notable uplink allocation dynamics: UL_NPRB swung between 7.7 and 50.6 (mean 23.9), including a large spike up to ~50.6. Current downlink PRBs were between 61.2 and 67.6 (mean 64.3), and current uplink PRBs were low, 0.15 to 3.3 (mean 1.3). DL PRB utilization ranged from 57.8% to 63.8% (mean 60.6%), while UL PRB utilization was minimal, 0.14% to 3.1% (mean 1.2%).

Traffic patterns were bursty. TX_Bytes oscillated with at least five sharp jumps/dips, ranging from 265,367 Bytes to 619,954 Bytes and averaging 441,396.2 Bytes; the largest observed drop reduced TX_Bytes to ~285,061 Bytes. RX_Bytes ranged from 2,588 Bytes to 17,814 Bytes with a mean of 5,720.1 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer varied between 368.9 KB and 1,524.2 KB (mean 509.5 KB). Packet counts reflected bursts: UL packets ranged 38 to 119 (mean 72.8), while DL packets ranged 0 to ~1,840 with a mean of 288.3 and experienced large spikes (e.g., to ~1,840 and ~1,179).

Protocol usage was overwhelmingly TCP: UL traffic was 100% TCP, and DL was TCP for ~85.9% of samples and UDP for ~0.8%. 

Implications: downlink PHY performance is stable with low DL BLER but modest DL MCS; uplink shows stronger SNR and MCS but higher BLER and intermittent high UL NPRB allocation — consistent with bursty uplink demand and occasional buffer growth.

**Diagnose Summary:**
- **Issue:** Severe Doppler shift causing periodic wireless signal and throughput instability.
- **Symptoms:** Periodic fluctuations in RSRP (3–8 dB) and uplink SNR (2–5 dB) at 2–3 Hz; downlink and uplink MCS decreased by 1–2 levels; multiplicative oscillations in transmitted/received bytes (factor 0.20–0.40) and PRBs allocated (factor 0.30–0.60) at 2–3 Hz.
- **Root Cause:** Rapid relative motion between the transmitter and receiver inducing Doppler effect.
- **Resolution:** Reduced source/receiver mobility, reoriented antennas for optimal alignment, and updated scheduling/adaptation algorithms to improve performance under mobility scenarios.

sample.description:
RSRP was consistently low, ranging between -121.0 dB and -116.0 dB. The average RSRP was -119.6 dB, indicating generally weak downlink signal strength.

Uplink modulation and resource behavior was highly variable. UL_MCS oscillated between 0 and 18 with a mean of 9.8, including at least four notable jumps and drops (the largest jump reached MCS 18). UL_NPRB varied from 5.0 to 88.8 PRBs with a mean of 20.1 and showed multiple large swings, the biggest being a sharp drop to 11.2 PRBs. UL_SNR stayed in a healthier range of 15.6 dB to 28.7 dB with a mean of 20.5 dB. UL_BLER ranged from 0.014 to 0.18 with a mean of 0.072, and experienced a spike up to 0.18 early in the trace. The Estimated_UL_Buffer spanned 1.5 KB to 6137.7 KB with a mean of 306.9 KB, indicating intermittent uplink queuing. UL_NumberOfPackets ranged from 1 to 197 with a mean of 56.1 packets. PRBs_UL_Current ranged from 0 to 80 (mean 3.6) and PRB_Utilization_UL ranged from 0% to 75% (mean 3.4%), with several large uplink allocation spikes (one reaching ~79.8 PRBs).

Downlink MCS and reliability were more stable but imperfect. DL_MCS stayed between 6.0 and 7.0 with a mean of 6.1. DL_BLER varied from 0.026 to 0.51 with a mean of 0.28 and exhibited two notable BLER jumps (peaks around 0.50–0.51), indicating intermittent downlink retransmissions. PRBs_DL_Current ranged from 13.8 to 67.3 with a mean of 49.9 and showed multiple pronounced drops; PRB_Utilization_DL ranged from 13.0% to 63.5% with a mean of 47.1%.

Throughput and traffic volumes displayed large swings. TX_Bytes (uplink traffic in Bytes) ranged from 92,829 to 441,465 with a mean of 299,427.1 Bytes and included at least eight large jumps/dips (the largest dip fell to 92,829 Bytes). RX_Bytes (downlink in Bytes) ranged from 228 to 16,669 with a mean of 4,575.4 Bytes. DL_NumberOfPackets spanned 0 to 620 with a mean of 176.3 packets.

Protocol usage was overwhelmingly TCP: DL_Protocol was TCP for 97.66% of timestamps and UL_Protocol was TCP for 100% of timestamps, with effectively no UDP observed.

Overall, the trace shows weak RSRP, moderate uplink SNR, bursty uplink resource allocation and traffic with intermittent large buffers, stable but occasionally lossy downlink MCS with elevated DL_BLER events, and predominantly TCP traffic.

Uplink modulation and scheduling showed volatility: UL MCS varied between 1.7 and 16.0 with a mean of 12.1, and experienced a sharp decline (about 12.97 points) down to ~1.66 late in the trace. UL NPRB swung widely from 5.0 to 44.9 resource blocks, mean 16.8, including at least one large spike to 44.9. PRBs allocated on the UL were low overall, ranging 0 to 9.8 with a mean of 1.6, and UL PRB utilization mirrored that (0 to 9.2, mean 1.5).

Downlink MCS was constrained, between 5.0 and 7.0 with a mean of 5.9. PRBs on the DL and DL PRB utilization were high and bursty: PRBs_DL_Current ranged 13.8 to 66.5, mean 48.2, and PRB_Utilization_DL ranged 13.0 to 62.8, mean 45.5; both series showed multiple large jumps (the largest DL jump raised PRBs by ~51.4 to ~66.3 and utilization by ~48.5 to ~62.5). 

Error performance: DL BLER was highly variable, spanning 0.014 to 1.0 with a mean of 0.37 and several prominent jumps and drops (including a fall of 0.9 down to 0.1 in one interval). UL BLER was lower and more stable, ranging 0.042 to 0.17 with a mean of 0.089.

Traffic and buffering exhibited large bursts. TX_Bytes varied from 92,829 Bytes to 445,114 Bytes with a mean of 287,812 Bytes and multiple large jumps/drops (the biggest drop reduced TX from ~445k down to ~108.8k). RX_Bytes ranged 138.0 Bytes to 8,706.0 Bytes with a mean of 3,802.3 Bytes. Estimated_UL_Buffer ranged 1.1 KB to 497.0 KB and averaged 193.0 KB. Packet counts reflected asymmetric load: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 93 (mean 48.1), while DL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 440 (mean 169.0).

Finally, transport was overwhelmingly TCP: DL_Protocol was TCP for 98.44% of timestamps and UL_Protocol for 99.22%.

The strong uplink traffic volume (measured in hundreds of thousands of bytes) contrasts with minimal downlink traffic (measured in thousands of bytes) and low downlink PRB allocation, despite high utilization. This discrepancy suggests a potential misconfiguration in downlink scheduling or an external factor causing downlink congestion, which can severely impact user experience in 5G networks.

Current downlink PRBs and DL PRB utilization both spiked to about 64.7 (range 0 to 65 PRBs; mean PRBs_DL_Current = 2.7), and PRB_Utilization_DL ranged 0 to 61% with a mean of 2.6%. UL PRBs and UL PRB utilization remained low: PRBs_UL_Current 0 to 4 (mean 0.14) and PRB_Utilization_UL 0 to 3.8% (mean 0.13%).

Traffic counters were bursty: TX_Bytes peaked around 388,121 Bytes (range 0 to 388,121 Bytes) with a mean of 16,200.9 Bytes, while RX_Bytes ranged 0 to 10,000 Bytes with a mean of 434.3 Bytes. The estimated uplink transmit buffer varied from 0 to 460 Kilobytes (mean 13.8 KB). Packet counts were low on average: UL_NumberOfPackets 0–20 (mean 0.92) and DL_NumberOfPackets 0–410 (mean 12.5).

Protocol usage was limited: downlink saw TCP in 1.56% of samples and UDP in 5.47%; uplink used TCP in 0.78% and UDP in 5.47% of timestamps.

sample.description:
The trace shows a weak downlink RF environment with intermittent improvements and bursts of uplink activity. RSRP ranged between -131.3 dB and -117.0 dB. The mean RSRP was -128.7 dB, with a notable increase of 14.29 dB reaching -117 dB around the 105–127s window. Uplink modulation and resource usage rose during the capture: UL_MCS varied from 5.0 to 15.0 with a mean of 6.6 and climbed to 15 around 101–127s; UL_NPRB ranged 12.3 to 44.9 with a mean of 17.7 and spiked to ~44.85 near 82–90s. UL_SNR was between 12.3 dB and 20.8 dB with an average of 14.6 dB.

Downlink MCS stayed low overall, ranging 0–7 with a mean of 1.1 and peaking at 7 during 101–127s. Downlink BLER was low in absolute terms, between 7.1e-05 and 0.014 with a mean of 0.0034, while uplink BLER was higher, ranging 0.06–0.20 with mean 0.15, indicating more uplink retransmission risk.

Traffic and buffering show uplink-dominant bursts: TX_Bytes varied from 67,914 Bytes to 448,843 Bytes with a mean of 154,561.8 Bytes and jumped sharply (~380,929 Bytes) to the peak around 106–122s. RX_Bytes ranged 1,292–16,686 Bytes with mean 2,777.4 Bytes. Estimated_UL_Buffer ranged 162.2–1,707.3 KB with a mean of 768.1 KB, consistent with queued uplink data during the TX spikes. UL_NumberOfPackets was 34.0–278.9 with mean 185.2, while DL_NumberOfPackets showed heavy variability (0 to 2,195.1 packets) with a mean of 506.8 and multiple large spikes (largest ~2,195 packets around 75–79s).

Scheduler and PRB metrics reflect asymmetric resource use: PRBs_DL_Current ranged 19.4–67.3 with mean 27.2 and increased to ~66.26 during 106–115s. PRBs_UL_Current stayed low at 0.22–4.6 with mean 0.76. DL PRB utilization was high and narrow at 57.8%–64.5% with mean 60.7%, whereas UL PRB utilization was low at 0.41%–5.3% with mean 1.4%.

Protocol usage was overwhelmingly TCP: DL used TCP for 76.56% of timestamps, and UL was TCP for 100% of timestamps (UDP 0% in both directions). Overall, the session exhibits uplink-heavy bursts with elevated UL BLER and buffers, limited DL radio quality and MCS, and high DL PRB utilization during peak intervals.

RSRP improved during the session, rising to a peak of -117.0 dB; overall RSRP ranged between -131.3 dB and -117.0 dB. The mean RSRP was -118.3 dB. Uplink modulation and radio quality were high: UL_MCS reached 15.0 (range 5.0 to 16.0) with a mean of 14.1, and UL_SNR varied between 12.8 dB and 21.0 dB with a mean of 18.9 dB. Downlink modulation was lower but near its maximum most of the time: DL_MCS peaked at 7.0 (range 0 to 7) with a mean of 6.3. DL_BLER remained very low, between 1e-05 and 0.01 with a mean of 0.0015, while UL_BLER was higher, between 0.06 and 0.18 with a mean of 0.11.

UL resource use showed intermittent heavy allocation: UL_NPRB spiked to 50.10 (range 11.6 to 50.1) with a mean of 18.3, whereas PRBs_UL_Current stayed low overall (range 0.3 to 7.3, mean 1.4) and PRB_Utilization_UL ranged from 0.41% to 7.5% with a mean of 2.8%. Downlink resources were heavily used: PRBs_DL_Current peaked around 66.26 (range 19.4 to 69.4) with a mean of 60.3, and PRB_Utilization_DL ran between 57.6% and 66.1% with a mean of 61.5%.

Traffic volumes show a dominant uplink data transfer episode and bursty downlink packets. TX_Bytes surged to 448,843 Bytes (overall range 67,914 to 470,288 Bytes) with a mean of 333,094 Bytes. RX_Bytes stayed relatively low, between 1,292 and 26,834 Bytes with a mean of 4,283.4 Bytes. The Estimated_UL_Buffer varied from 162.2 KB to 1,669.9 KB with a mean of 477.0 KB. Packet counts reflect burstiness: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged from 34.0 to 231.4 with a mean of 105.7, while DL_NumberOfPackets spiked up to 1,805 (range 0 to 1,805) with a mean of 327.4; several pronounced DL packet jumps were observed.

Protocol usage was almost entirely TCP: DL_Protocol was TCP for 88.28% of timestamps, and UL_Protocol was TCP for 100.00% of timestamps. Overall, the profile indicates strong uplink radio performance and capacity bursts on UL resources with persistent high downlink PRB utilization despite modest downlink throughput and very low DL BLER.

Uplink and downlink MCS decreased (5–15 units). PRBs for downlink (30–80%) and uplink (50–80%) decreased. Transmitted and received bytes declined logarithmically. Uplink buffer backlog grew exponentially. Uplink packet count rose (50–200%), downlink packet count increased (30–100%).
- **Root Cause:** Hardware malfunction due to antenna failure impeding signal transmission and reception.
- **Resolution:** Antenna hardware was inspected, faulty components replaced, and network performance monitored to confirm restoration.

Therefore, this pattern is consistent with 'Stationary'.

sample.description:
RSRP showed substantial variability: values ranged between -136.1 dB and -116.0 dB. The average RSRP was -127.8 dB, with a notable short-term peak near -116 dB and a deeper trough around -133.4 dB later in the trace. 

UL_MCS varied between 7.0 and 15.0 with a mean of 9.6. DL_MCS spanned 0 to 7 with an average of 2.3, indicating generally low downlink modulation efficiency compared with uplink. 

DL_BLER remained very low, ranging from 0 to 0.0048 with a mean of 0.00092. UL_BLER ranged from 0.053 to 0.25 with a mean of 0.10, and experienced a dip to around 0.05 during one interval. 

UL_NPRB ranged from 10.4 to 23.9 with a mean of 16.6. UL_SNR varied between 4.8 dB and 20.7 dB and averaged 10.8 dB; there was a transient high near 20.7 dB and a later low close to 5 dB. 

UL traffic volume (TX_Bytes) was highly bursty: values ranged from 53,739 Bytes to 445,114 Bytes and the mean was 295,066.5 Bytes, with a large jump to roughly 443,817 Bytes during a peak interval. DL traffic (RX_Bytes) was much smaller, ranging from 1,036 Bytes to 7,802 Bytes with a mean of 3,517 Bytes. 

The Estimated_UL_Buffer varied between 142.2 KB and 1,262.2 KB with a mean of 387.3 KB, reflecting intermittent uplink queuing. DL PRBs in use (PRBs_DL_Current) ranged from 35 to 67 with a mean of 46.1. PRBs_UL_Current ranged from 0.068 to 2.9 with a mean of 0.65. Downlink PRB utilization was relatively stable between 57.8% and 63.8% (mean 60.7%), while uplink PRB utilization was low, between 0.23% and 2.8% (mean 1.2%). 

UL_NumberOfPackets ranged from 55 to 147.5 with a mean of 95.7. DL_NumberOfPackets was highly spiky, ranging from 0 to 1,811 with a mean of 436.7 and showing multiple prominent jumps, including a peak at 1,811 packets. 

Protocol usage was dominated by TCP: DL traffic was TCP for 79.69% of timestamps (UDP negligible), and UL traffic was TCP for 100% of timestamps. 

Overall, the trace shows stronger instantaneous uplink radio conditions (higher UL_MCS and transient UL_SNR peaks) and heavy, bursty uplink throughput with intermittent buffering, while downlink exhibits low modulation, low BLER, modest PRB load, and spiky packet arrivals.

sample.description:
Over the trace, downlink reference signal received power (RSRP) improved notably, rising by about 16 dB to a peak near -95.8 dBm; overall RSRP ranged between -112.2 dBm and -95.8 dBm. The mean RSRP was -100.2 dBm.

Uplink modulation and coding efficiency increased, with UL MCS jumping to a maximum of 15 (range 7.0 to 15.0); UL MCS averaged 12.9. Downlink MCS also climbed to 7, with values spanning 0 to 7 and a mean of 5.1. Downlink block error rate remained very low (range 0 to 0.0081, mean 0.0011). Uplink BLER rose at one point to 0.22, with UL BLER ranging from 0.064 to 0.22 and averaging 0.13.

Uplink SNR showed a strong improvement, peaking around 21.1 dB after a ~14.5 dB jump; UL SNR ranged from 5.2 dB to 22.6 dB and had a mean of 16.8 dB. Uplink NPRB usage varied between 11.4 and 38.9 PRBs, mean 21.5. Current downlink PRBs increased sharply to about 67, with PRBs_DL_Current spanning 12.2 to 67.3 and a mean of 50.3. PRBs allocated on uplink were low (range 0.094 to 3.5, mean 1.2).

Downlink PRB utilization surged to roughly 90%, with PRB_Utilization_DL ranging from 56.8% to 91.1% and averaging 75.9%. Uplink PRB utilization stayed minimal (0.18% to 5.3%, mean 1.7%).

Traffic shows asymmetric behavior: transmit bytes experienced a large spike to ~452k Bytes then dropped to a low near 240.8k Bytes; TX_Bytes ranged from 228,880 Bytes to 452,412 Bytes and averaged 282,262.6 Bytes. Received bytes were much smaller, ranging 1,888 Bytes to 9,297 Bytes with a mean of 3,182.1 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer varied between 139.5 KB and 1,236.7 KB, mean 509.8 KB. Packet counts reflected this asymmetry: UL packets ranged 18.3 to 317.3 (mean 70.7), while DL packet counts spiked to about 2,149 packets and overall ranged from 0 to ~2,100 with a mean of 296.9.

Protocol usage was dominated by TCP: DL was TCP for 97.66% of timestamps (UDP negligible), and UL was TCP for 100% of timestamps.

Uplink and downlink modulation showed generally good link quality: UL MCS ranged from 12.0 to 16.0 with a mean of 14.4, while DL MCS was constant at 7.0. Downlink BLER spanned 0.012 to 0.063 with a mean of 0.031. Uplink BLER ranged from 0.028 to 0.16 and averaged 0.093.

Resource allocation and utilization exhibited intermittent peaks. UL NPRB varied between 5.0 and 34.6 with a mean of 12.0, including a notable spike up to 34.6. DL PRBs current ranged from 0 to 50 with a mean of 16.6 and showed at least three distinct jumps, one reaching 48.1. DL PRB utilization ranged from 0 to 47 with a mean of 15.7 and experienced multiple large spikes (largest ~45.4). UL PRBs current and utilization were low, ranging 0 to 4 (mean 1.1) and 0 to 3.7 (mean 1.0), respectively.

Traffic and buffer metrics showed bursty uplink transmission and modest downlink volumes. TX_Bytes ranged from 177.0 Bytes to 264,004.0 Bytes, mean 93,320.4 Bytes, with several pronounced jumps (largest jump to ~248,567 Bytes). RX_Bytes ranged from 46.0 Bytes to 11,267.0 Bytes with a mean of 3,561.6 Bytes. Estimated UL buffer varied between 0 Kilobytes and 760 Kilobytes, averaging 158.7 Kilobytes. UL packet counts ranged 0 to 66 (mean 23.8) and DL packet counts ranged 0 to 180 (mean 59.2).

sample.description:
Over the trace the downlink reference signal received power weakened notably, reaching a minimum of -97.0 dB and a maximum of -87.0 dB. The average RSRP was -88.7 dB, with an observed drop of about 8.96 dB between t≈97 and t≈123. Uplink SNR showed a sharp decline as well, falling to a low of 6.8 dB and peaking at 24.3 dB; its mean value was 19.7 dB, and a drop of ~16.75 dB occurred between t≈102 and t≈109. Uplink MCS increased to a peak of 15 (range 9.0–15.0) with a mean of 9.2, including a jump of 6 MCS levels late in the trace. Downlink MCS remained stable at 7.0.

Error rates stayed very low: DL_BLER ranged from 0 to 0.023 with a mean of 0.00086, and UL_BLER ranged from 0 to 0.015 with a mean of 0.00049. Resource allocation was generally minimal: DL PRBs used varied between 0 and 64 (mean 2.5), with PRB utilization on DL spanning 0–93% and averaging 3.6%; UL PRBs ranged 0–8.8 (mean 0.19) and UL utilization 0–13% (mean 0.26). PRBs on DL spiked late in the trace by ~64.4 to a high of 64.4, and DL utilization rose by ~92.95 to a high of 92.95 over the same period.

Traffic was bursty and uplink-dominant during the peak: TX_Bytes reached 268,018 Bytes (range 0–268,018 Bytes) with a mean of 8,350.4 Bytes, while RX_Bytes varied from 11 to 4,169 Bytes with a mean of 260.1 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer ranged from 0 to 1,200 Kilobytes and averaged 26.3 KB. Packet counts were low: UL packets 0–7 (mean 0.055) and DL packets 0–2 (mean 0.047). Finally, TCP was observed intermittently — on the downlink for 3.91% of timestamps and on the uplink for 0.78% — with essentially no UDP traffic.

- **Issue:** Excessively frequent handovers due to a faulty handover algorithm.
- **Symptoms:** Periodic fluctuations in Reference Signal Received Power (2.00–5.00 amplitude, 0.1000–0.3000 Hz); periodic uplink Signal-to-Noise Ratio fluctuations (1.00–3.00 amplitude, 0.1000–0.3000 Hz); increased block error rates on both uplink and downlink (30%–150%); reduced transmitted and received byte counts (10%–50% decrease); increased uplink buffer backlog (50%–200%); increased uplink/downlink packet counts (50%–200%).
- **Root Cause:** Malfunctioning handover algorithm causing excessive, unnecessary cell transitions.
- **Resolution:** Optimized handover algorithm parameters and thresholds to reduce handover frequency and stabilize network performance.
